overview: The two phases of the uterine (endometrial) cycle, corresponding to the ovarian follicular and luteal phases respectively.
genZNote: Proliferative phase: the lining is under construction. Secretory phase: the lining is furnished and stocked, waiting for a tenant.

aspects.label: Driving Hormone
aspects.valueA: Estrogen, causing the endometrium to thicken and regenerate.
aspects.valueB: Progesterone, causing endometrial glands to secrete nutrient-rich fluid.

aspects.label: Corresponds to Ovarian Cycle Phase
aspects.valueA: Corresponds to the follicular phase of the ovarian cycle.
aspects.valueB: Corresponds to the luteal phase of the ovarian cycle.

aspects.label: Purpose
aspects.valueB: Prepares the endometrium to support a fertilised egg, if implantation occurs.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The uterine cycle (proliferative-secretory-menstrual) and ovarian cycle (follicular-luteal) run in parallel, driven by the same hormonal shifts.
overlay.memoryTrick: Proliferative = building up (estrogen). Secretory = glands secreting, ready for pregnancy (progesterone).
overlay.commonMisconception: These are phases of the uterine lining cycle, not the ovary itself — don't confuse them with the follicular/luteal phase terminology used for the ovary.
